text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: High error rates and partial availability in us-east-1a for inference-serving cluster redwood-infer-prod. 5xx spike + target registration flapping on NLB. Pager sent to #incidents and paging policy: oncall

maya (oncall): paging in. seeing 500s on /v1/generate from multiple customers in us-east-1a. console shows increased RequestCount and TargetHealth errors on NLB: redwood-nlb-eu-prod-a.

aj (sre): confirming. CloudWatch shows ENI network RX drops on a subset of instances and EC2 health status 'impaired' for 3 instances. Could be underlying host network or AZ fabric.

maya (oncall): tagging customers impacted: cust-alpha (hosted), cust-b2b (dedicated in us-east-1a), several small PLG callers. Li-chen can you flag CS?

li-chen (cs): on it, pushing proactive note to affected customers with temporary mitigation guidance and link to status page.

aj (sre): quick triage steps: 1) remove unhealthy targets from NLB target group to stop noisy retries 2) shift traffic to us-east-1b and us-east-1c via routing policy 3) spin up replacement instances in other AZs if capacity available.

maya (oncall): executing step 1 now.

aj (sre): command: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456:targetgroup/redwood-infer-tg/abcd --targets Id=i-0abc1234,i-0def5678```

incident-bot: Action logged by maya (oncall): deregistered 3 targets from redwood-infer-tg (us-east-1a).

aj (sre): seeing NLB target health improve but client 5xx persists for remaining capacity due to cross-AZ network variance. Getting repeated InsufficientInstanceCapacity on launch attempts in us-east-1a: "InsufficientInstanceCapacity: We currently do not have sufficient capacity" in the API responses.

tim (platform): initiating cross-AZ reroute: updating traffic policy to prefer us-east-1b for next 30m, and enabling overflow to our warm pool in us-east-1c. Will update infra DNS and traffic manager.

aj (sre): DNS change: updating Route53 weighted records for inference.api.redwood.com to divert 70% to us-east-1b, 20% to us-east-1c, 10% remain in 1a for canary. Command: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://r53-failover.json``` (r53-failover.json contained new weights)

aws-status-bot: AWS reported an event in us-east-1a: "Network connectivity interruptions affecting some EC2 instances and ENI detach/attach errors". Root cause under investigation.

maya (oncall): mitigation update: traffic shifted. Observability: latency for us-east-1 traffic stable at ~80ms, error rate dropped from 18% to 2% overall. Dedicated customers on reserved capacity in 1a still seeing partial failures if pinned to 1a.

li-chen (cs): note to affected dedicated customers: recommending temporary failover to cross-AZ model variants or use Dedicated failover option. Preparing playbook for accounts with compliance constraints.

aj (sre): additional step: replace impaired instances with instances launched in other AZs and update autoscaling groups to prefer subnets in 1b/1c. Avoid launching more in 1a until capacity stabilizes. Also increasing connection draining timeout on NLB to 120s to reduce 502/504 spikes during target swaps.

maya (oncall): running kubectl/drain against pods on the 3 impaired hosts to move work to healthy hosts: ```kubectl drain ip-10-0-1-23.us-east-1a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Logs show graceful termination but some requests in-flight returned 502.

aj (sre): note: observed one customer report of inference token loss during failover. Recommending retriable client logic and adding a transient-error header in responses so SDKs can auto-retry non-idempotent requests safely.

incident-bot: Status update posted: Partial outage in us-east-1a affecting subset of inference hosts; elevated error rates mitigated via cross-AZ reroute. Follow-up link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1763234567

maya (oncall): handing off to aj (sre) for overnight monitoring. aj, can you confirm any remaining impacted services and run periodic checks on NLB target health and Route53 weights?

aj (sre): taking over. Will monitor for 3 hours and escalate to platform team if capacity doesn't return. Scheduled check-ins at +15m, +45m, +120m.

li-chen (cs): customers notified, some asked for ETA on dedicated failover. Sharing internal runbook and will coordinate one-off failovers where allowed.

aws-status-bot: AWS updated: "As of T+40m, EC2 host networking event shows improvement; customers may see restored capacity in us-east-1a gradually. Instances that were impaired must be replaced to recover".

aj (sre): plan: continue to avoid new launches in 1a, replace impaired instances when safe, keep traffic policy favoring 1b/1c for next 2 hours, and then slowly reintroduce 1a once three consecutive successful instance launches observed.

maya (oncall): thanks team, passing primary incident ticket to postmortem queue. I'll add initial timeline and customer impact summary. Oncall handoff complete :white_check_mark:

li-chen (cs): adding notes to customer tickets and logging who was impacted + mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Incident moved to "mitigated" state. Postmortem assigned to aj (sre) and tim (platform).

aj (sre): quick logs snippet for postmortem: ```[2026-03-15T02:12:45Z] ENI RxDrops detected on eni-0a1b2c3d - detach/attach errors - kernel logs: "Failed to sync device"``` Will capture CloudTrail + ENI metrics and NLB target health timeline.

maya (oncall): last check before sign-off: overall client error rate ~1.8%, US-east total throughput restored to 95% of baseline. Passing to aj for cleanup.

aj (sre): acknowledged. I'll post RCA draft and mitigation recommendations (route53 automated failover playbook, improved warm-pool capacity, better instance provisioning spread) in #postmortems later tonight.

li-chen (cs): closing customer comms loop once RCA available.

incident-bot: Thread closed by aj (sre).
